title: Durable Target orchestration handoff
intent: Turn the committed native Target outbox fact into a durable, inspectable Temporal TargetWorkflow handoff without moving business truth or Graph Engine authority into Temporal.
scope: Add a Go outbox dispatcher, a versioned minimal TargetWorkflow, safe delivery leases and retries, a pinned local Temporal runtime, tests, operational documentation, and inspectable evidence for the Target-created event path.
non_goals: Implement Graph Engine node activation, RunWorkflow, Execution Gateway, or Runner execution
Write Target business state from a Temporal Workflow
Create a TypeScript Workflow or a second outbox consumer
Expose orchestration status as a product-facing source of truth
Design production Temporal topology, multi-region failover, or managed-cloud provisioning
Broaden the Go replatform beyond the approved Target orchestration slice
Commit, merge, deploy, or release without explicit approval
acceptance_criteria: The Go worker registers explicitly versioned Workflow, signal, query, and task-queue names and uses a stable Workflow ID derived from Workspace and Target IDs.

The dispatcher claims committed outbox events with a fencing claim token, bounded lease, per-aggregate ordering, and skip-locked concurrency without holding a database transaction across a Temporal call.
SignalWithStart delivers the outbox event ID and stable aggregate identifiers, and the dispatcher marks delivery only when the matching claim still owns the row.
Retryable delivery failures return the event to pending with bounded exponential backoff; expired leases are recoverable; unsupported or exhausted events become inspectable failed rows.
TargetWorkflow keeps only orchestration state, deduplicates redelivery, exposes a versioned query, and uses Continue-As-New at a bounded history threshold.
Postgres remains authoritative for Target facts and outbox delivery state; Temporal downtime leaves committed events recoverable rather than rolling back or mutating Target facts.
Local development uses an explicitly pinned Temporal dev-server image and separate Domain API and orchestration-worker processes.
Workflow, dispatcher, lease recovery, retry, dead-letter, duplicate delivery, replay, configuration, and real Temporal handoff checks produce inspectable evidence.
Canonical architecture and development documentation state the implemented boundary without claiming Graph Engine or Run execution is complete.
